title: Reject an empty custom timestep list with a clear ValueError
request: Make passing an empty custom timestep list produce a clear error while preserving valid inputs.
proposed_approach: The engineer asked whether an empty list could be replaced with [999]. Treat that as a hypothesis and reject a silent default if library guidance prefers a clear error.

criteria.text: DDPMScheduler.set_timesteps and the copied DDPMParallelScheduler.set_timesteps raise ValueError when timesteps is an empty list; the existing both-argument conflict error still wins when both arguments are supplied.
A descending custom list and a single-element custom list keep their values on CPU when no device is requested.
Passing num_inference_steps and timesteps together still raises the existing mutual-exclusion ValueError.
Calling set_timesteps with only num_inference_steps still builds a descending schedule of that length.

exclusions: Do not change scheduler numerical updates
Do not add a shared validation helper or new dependency
Do not silently replace an empty list with a default schedule
